topic: Pain on the outside of the ankle (peroneal tendons)

slides.headline: Ache along the outside of your ankle?
slides.sub: Often the peroneal tendons. Here's what usually helps them settle.

slides.title: Meet the peroneals
slides.body: These two tendons run behind the bony bump on the outside of your ankle. They help steady your foot, especially on uneven ground, trails and sand, and when you change direction quickly.

slides.title: Why they get cranky
slides.body: Often it's a jump in load: more running, a new trail, long beach walks in soft sand or a lingering ankle sprain. Feet that tend to roll outward can add extra strain as well.

slides.title: Settle, then strengthen
slides.body: Ease back on whatever flared it without stopping everything. Then build up with band exercises turning the foot outward, calf raises and balance work. Tendons usually respond well to gradual, steady loading.

slides.title: Check your footwear
slides.body: Worn-out shoes or very soft, unstable sneakers can make things worse. A supportive, well-fitting shoe for walking and training is a good starting point while it settles.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A clicking or snapping feeling behind the ankle bone, swelling that doesn't ease, an ankle that keeps giving way, or pain after a bad roll deserve an assessment.

slides.headline: Outside-ankle pain hanging around?
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios check your ankle, footwear and training, then build a loading plan to keep you moving. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Ache on the outside of your ankle after beach walks or trail runs? The peroneal tendons are a common reason.

These tendons steady your foot on uneven ground. They often get cranky after a jump in load, like more running, soft sand walks or a new trail, or after an old ankle sprain that never quite settled.

Most people do well by easing back without stopping altogether, then gradually strengthening with band work, calf raises and balance drills. Supportive shoes help too.

Snapping behind the ankle bone, swelling that won't ease or an ankle that keeps giving way are worth getting checked.

story.headline: Outside-ankle ache?
story.body: Ease back a little, don't stop completely, and start band work and calf raises. Tendons like steady loading.
